comments.text: H.TIL's 128 tiles, laid out as LAND.TIL's: pixel row r of tile t has its left byte at $4080 + $100 * r + t and its right byte at $4000 + $100 * r + t. Tiles 0-15 the Manchi (0-7 calm, 8-15 angry), 16-27 brush, 28-39 brush burnt, 40-56 rock, 57-65 and 114-119 water, 66-84 bare ground, 85-92 the trooper, 93 the shot, 95-97 a mound rising and 98 the mound, 100-112 the drop ship. Rows 0-3 from here
The island tiles' pixel rows 4-7, in the same layout
The island tiles' pixel rows 8-11
The island tiles' pixel rows 12-14; row 15 from $4F00
The island tiles' last pixel row, right bytes; draw_chart's patched load at $8711 was left pointing here
The last pixel row's left bytes, where draw_chart's load at $871A was left

Each island tile's kind, with the bits of LAND.TIL's: the Manchi's even tiles $81, brush $10 (it slows a Manchi's sight and burns when shot), burnt brush and bare ground 0, rock $84 (it blocks the way and sight), water $A0 ($A8 for tile $72), the trooper's tiles $85 and $04, the mound $80, the drop ship $80 and $84, and its hatch, tile $67, $0C (it hides the trooper standing in it, from sight and from the chart)
Tile $7E's kind, where draw_brackets' right-half mask pointer was left in this load
Tile $7F's kind, where the right-half pattern pointer was left in this load
Each island tile's two colours for draw_chart's screen matrix: the high nybble for bit pair 01, the low for 10 (brush $5F, green on light grey)
Tile $7E's colours; draw_brackets' left-half mask pointer was left here in this load
Tile $7F's colours, the last byte of H.TIL, where the left-half pattern pointer was left in this load

The island, 32 by 32 tiles of H.TIL, a row at a time from the top (Y = 31): the tile at X, Y is at $5100 + 32 * (31 - Y) + X. Water all round, brush and rock across it, and the drop ship at columns 16-19, rows 12-15, its hatch at 18, 14. The shot writes burnt brush back into it ($5B5F); hive_menu loads it afresh for every game
Row 4 of the island's grid (Y = 27), where sector_kind's patched LDY at $2F95 was left
2 in H.MAP, a byte no code reads (bases have 1, system maps 0), then zeros: the island has no name
Each of the 32 entries' column ($FF free): entry 0 the trooper, who lands at 19, 14 beside the ship; entry 1 his shot; 2-31 the mounds and Manchi, cleared at each drop
The shot's column, $7F (off the map, so never drawn) while none flies
Each entry's row, counted from the bottom: the trooper starts on row 14
The shot's row while it flies
Each entry's flags as in a base map: $80 the trooper and the mounds (solid, still), $81 a wandering Manchi, $83 a chasing one, plus the heading in bits 3-4 and the still bit 5
Each entry's picture: $55 the trooper, $5D the shot, $62 a mound, 0 a calm Manchi and 8 an angry one ($FF none)
Each entry's type: 1 a Manchi, $FF anything else (the trooper, the shot, a mound)
The entries' extra bytes, zeros in H.MAP; nothing in HCODE reads them, and remove_entry clears them
The entries' messages, all $FFFF (none) in H.MAP
The high byte of the trooper's message word
Zero in H.MAP: a base map's kind byte, which HCODE never reads; zeros run on to $5617
Zero here; in a base map the column where a visitor turns up, read only on arriving at a base
Zero here; in a base map the visitor's row, in a system map the danger level
Each entry's action byte: for a Manchi, the number of the mound entry that bred it (hive_breed_one), so that a mound keeps no more than four
Entry 8's mound number; in a system map the bases' map file names start here ($16B2)
Entry 9's mound number; in a system map a base file name's second character
Entry 10's mound number; in a system map a base file name's third character
Entry 24's mound number; in a system map the gates' data starts here ($7188)
Entry 25's mound number; a system map gate's second byte
Entry 26's mound number; a gate's third byte
Entry 27's mound number; a gate's fourth byte
Zero in H.MAP, where a base map has its cargo prices (cargo_price); unused by HIVE!
Zero in H.MAP, where a base map's cargo availability lies; the file's zeros run to $56FF

HIVE!'s start, called by the cabinet's action (act_hive, $AAE5). The base map's entries ($5500-$56FF) are saved at $6200, the cabinet's picture H.PAC is shown (load_picture 3) and H.TIL is loaded over LAND.TIL at $4000
The LDA's operand; when TALK is loaded here, the talk interpreter reads $5701 as the high byte of script 0's offset

The cabinet's menu. H.MAP is loaded to $5100, again before every game, so each starts on the same untouched island; the chart is set to show it and "Welcome to HIVE!, the arcade game of the century... INSERT CREDIT, QUIT GAME" printed ($CF33). INSERT CREDIT takes 1 credit and starts a game; QUIT GAME, or INSERT CREDIT with no credit, leaves

Back to the base: its screen ($A55D), its map file (the name kept at $0778) loaded back to $5100, the chart put back on it, and the entries saved at $6200 copied over the fresh file's, so the people and items stand where they were

A game, from combat drop 1 ($D0 keeps the drop's number). Each drop: "Combat drop #n is under way. Prepare to deploy on planet's surface." ($CF31, $CF30), a key, and the drop played ($5900) at level n with 3 * n mounds to destroy. A drop won says "Drop successful!" ($CF2F), waits ten ticks, and the next begins

The trooper was caught on drop n. From drop 5 on he wins (n - 4) * 8 credits: "You have displayed extreme valor by surviving more than four combat drops. The Star Force rewards your feat with a n Cr prize. Congratulations trooper!" ($CF2E, $CF2D). Before that: "A pair of Manchi grab hold of your battle suit and rip you in half. You lose." ($CF32). A key, the view cleared, and the menu again
Fills the chart window with tile $7C, far from the map, and draws it; then prints the ten spaces at $584C over the MOUNDS line (column 15, row 16)
Ten spaces and a zero, printed over the MOUNDS line between games
"H.TIL", the tiles' file name, zero-ended; "H.MAP" follows at $585D
"H.MAP", the island's map file, zero-ended
Zeros to $58FF, filling HCODE's first part out to the page; no code reads them

One combat drop, at level X ($CE) with A mounds to destroy ($CC). Every map entry but the trooper (0) and his shot (1) is taken off, the next mound's timer ($CD) set to 30 and the count shown. Then each pass: the Manchi and the trooper move ($5D00), the shot flies ($5ADC), the recall is checked ($5BCD), a mound may rise ($59BA), every 32nd pass each mound breeds ($5A74), the chart is drawn around the trooper, a tick waited, the Manchi's mood set ($5976) and the trooper's fate checked ($5947). It ends with A = $FF (minus) when the drop is won, 0 when he is caught

The trooper is caught when two Manchi at once stand next to him (entry_distance under 2, diagonals included; one alone does nothing): the chart drawn, sound 9, and the drop ended with A = 0, the caller's return dropped
The Manchi's mood: when any Manchi can see the trooper ($5BF8), every Manchi gets motion kind 3, chasing, and picture 8, the angry Manchi; otherwise all get kind 1, wandering, and picture 0

Raises mounds. With five on the map, nothing. Otherwise the timer ($CD) counts down, twice as fast while there are none, and at zero it is set again from the level: 150 - 8 * level, worked out in one byte, is kept only when the subtraction goes below zero (the BCC at $59E4, which looks reversed), otherwise 1; then a random 0-90 is added with random_upto's carry, which is set only when it gives 90. So every level up to 18 waits 1 to 90 passes, or 92, and from level 19 the wrapped result is kept. Then a mound is put on a random square that holds no entry, is not the drop ship's hatch (18, 14), and whose tile has none of kind bits 7, 4 and 5 (no water, rock or brush)
The square's tile must neither block (bit 7) nor carry bits 4-5 (brush and water); the hatch's tile ($67, kind $0C) passes this test, hence its own check above

A free entry becomes the mound: its square, picture $62 and flags $80 (solid, still); sound 10. When the square is in the chart window, the mound is shown rising: tiles $5F, $60 and $61 in its cell in turn, two ticks each

One frame of the rising mound: the chart refilled around the trooper ($5BE4), the tile number in $C7 put in the mound's cell of the chart buffer ($FA00 plus the cell index in $95), the chart drawn and two ticks waited. Called for $5F and $60, then run on into for $61

Every 32nd pass each mound (picture $62) breeds: when fewer than four entries carry its number in their action byte ($5618), one more Manchi is made on the mound's square ($5A9C). A dead Manchi's byte is cleared (remove_entry), so a mound breeds again as its brood is shot

One Manchi for mound $C6, unless a Manchi still stands on the mound's square: a free entry gets the square, the mound's number in its action byte ($5618), flags $81 (solid, wandering) and type 1; its picture is set on the next pass ($5976)

The trooper's shot. A nonzero step X, Y from the keys becomes the aim ($CA, $CB). ESC waits for a key, a pause. Space or the fire button fires: sound 8, and the shot (entry 1) leaves the trooper's square and flies up to five squares along the aim, drawn at each

A square whose tile blocks (kind bit 7: water, rock, the ship) stops the shot. Brush (kind $10) is burnt: its tile in the grid at $5100 + 32 * (31 - y) + x becomes the one 12 on ($1C-$27, kind 0), and the shot flies on

The entries on the square ($3030): the first Manchi there (type 1) is killed (remove_entry) and stops the shot. A mound (picture $62) is destroyed only from the square next to it, the first of the five, with the count lowered and shown again ($5BA9); further off it just stops the shot
The shot's column set to $7F, off the map, so it is not drawn
Prints "MOUNDS: " and the number left ($CC) at column 15, row 16; at none, "! RECALL !" and sound 3: the trooper must get back to the drop ship
The drop is won when no mound is left and the trooper stands on the drop ship's hatch, the square 18, 14: the caller's return is dropped and A = $FF goes back to the drop's caller
Fills the chart window around the trooper (cells off the map get tile $39, water) and puts the map's entries in ($2F9C)

Carry clear when Manchi Y can see the trooper. A line is walked from the Manchi a square at a time, each step a single move across and down toward him, with five steps to spend: a tile with kind bit 2 (rock, parts of the ship, and the hatch he can stand in) hides him, and brush (kind $10) costs two more steps. Carry set when the steps run out first
"MOUNDS: ", zero-ended, then "! RECALL !" at $5C6A; zeros from $5C75 to the page's end, which no code reads

The Manchi's moves and the trooper's. Each Manchi (type 1) moves on a pass when a random 0 to level + 10 is 9 or more, so (level + 2) times in level + 11: by its motion kind's routine from the table at $5D95 (kind 1 $5D74, kind 3 move_chase in SEG1), patched into the JSR at $5D30, and its heading set. Then the keys or joystick: unless fire is held the trooper steps (try_step, sliding along a wall when blocked), his heading and still bit set. Returns the key in A and the step in X, Y
The low byte of the JSR's address, patched with the Manchi's move routine
The high byte of the patched JSR's address
Motion kind 1, a wandering Manchi: one sharing its square with another entry always takes a random step; one alone does so one pass in four
The last two bytes of the JMP: hive_moves reads the motion table at $5D95 + 2 * kind, so kind 0 would read them
The JMP's high byte, read as kind 0's high byte

The motion kinds' routines, a word each from kind 1: $5D74 wander, $5D73 (an RTS: kind 2 stands still, never given here) and $A785 (move_chase in SEG1, kind 3). Zeros follow to $5DFF; no code reads them
